correctness.rationale: For a nonzero unital simple ring R, J(R)=0. The 2026 source proves simplicity and sqrt-Delta-fineness of every M_n(R). Leroy--Matczuk prove Delta(M_n(R))=J(M_n(R))=M_n(J(R)) for n>=2, hence Delta(M_n(R))=0 and sqrt(Delta(M_n(R))) is exactly the nilpotent set. The defining decomposition is therefore an ordinary fine decomposition. The E_11 corner is explicitly full and isomorphic to R, proving the Morita consequence.

value.rationale: The result sharply reduces the 2026 open question to the base ring by proving every full matrix amplification of size at least two is already classically fine. It also shows that any counterexample would simultaneously disprove the longstanding full-corner/Morita-invariance question for fine rings, giving a motivated structural bridge rather than a routine restatement.
